title:
Base type for all configurations.

For quick reference guide scroll to the bottom of this chapter, but it is recommended to get familiar with nuances
of how config framework works in C3 AI Platform. See the topic, "Overview of C3 AI Configuration Framework"
(config-framework.c3doc.md).

Different configurations can be classified in following buckets:

* `Singleton` configuration - only one instance exists regardless of the context - for example, `DevEnvironmentConfig`

* `Sub Type` configuration - an instance of a configuration exists per sub-type of this Config - typically none of
  the sub-types would be abstract but if one is then while it would not have a configuration instance other methods
  do still make sense. Note that this is not the same as `Singleton` - a type that is configured may not be a
  `Singleton` - for example, `KvStoreConfig`

* `UserSingleton` configuration - a single instance per user - for example, `JupyterConfig`

* `Identified` configuration - configured by `id` of what it is for - for example, `ServerConfig`

* `Named` configuration - configured by `name` of what it is for - for example, `DatastoreConfig`

* _--- custom ---_ - configured by custom logic - for example, `CloudResource`

#isSingleInstance and #hasSubTypes methods can be used to identify specific kind of the Config type and
#listConfigKeys can be used for all existing configurations.

Additionally, configuration instances are hierarchical. The final configuration is determined by merging instances
starting from `seed configuration` and following order defined by {@see ConfigOverride} enum.

When merging configuration by default fields defined by more specific configuration replace ones defined by more
generic ones. However, Ann.Config#merge annotation can alter this behavior.

Optional minimum and maximum configuration override levels are set per configuration type using
Ann.Config#minOverride and Ann.Config#maxOverride.

Optional seed configuration can be authored as part of the application package under metadata path:
`<repo>/<pkg>/config/<config folder>/<config key>.json`.

Config Folder name by default is configuration type name; however, it can be overridden using Ann.Config#folder.
See also #configFolder method.

Config Key is determined by configuration kind as outlined above. That is, it is configuration type name in case of
`Singleton` and `Sub Type` configuration or `id` or `name` field values in case of `Identifiable` and `Nameable`.
See also #configKey method.

Note that there is a reserved config key '_' which if present will be used as the bases of all other configuration values.
That is, if `_.json` config exists then it will be loaded first and then `<config key>.json` will be merged into it.

Finally, configuration file content is actually a json {@link Template}. Merging of json templates based on rules
described above happens before formatting it and binding variables as defined by #templateBindings.

Note that if configuration contains nested structure those types need to mixin ConfigChild.

*Quick reference guide*: since recommended pattern is to use {@link Configurable} Type instead low level
{@link Config} examples below assume `myConfigurable` is an instance of `{@link Configurable}`.

* Get a configuration or secret value:
  ```
  myConfigurable.config().configValue('path.to.my.value');
  myConfigurable.config().configValue('path.to.my.value', true);
  myConfigurable.config().configValue('arry[17].field');
  myConfigurable.config().secretValue('map['key'].field');
  myConfigurable.config().secretValue('arryWithUniqueId['<id value>'].field');
  myConfigurable.config().secretValue('arryWithUniqueName['<name value>'].field');
  ```

* Set a configuration or secret value:
  ```
  myConfigurable.config().setConfigValue('path.to.my.value', '<my value>');
  myConfigurable.config().setSecretValue('path.to.my.value', '<my value>', ConfigOverride.CLUSTER);
  ```

If you really think you need to use {@link Config} Type directly, then replace `myConfigurable.config()` with one of:
 - `MyConfig.inst`
 - `MyConfig.forId`
 - `MyConfig.forName`
based of the kind of MyConfig.


@see Configurable
@see ConfigChild
